meta.title: Health, Creative and Performing Arts (Physical Education and Arts)
meta.issuing_body: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (MoPSE), in collaboration with the Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)
curriculum_periods_covered: 2015 - 2022 (Visual and Performing Arts; Physical Education, Sport and Mass Displays - as separate learning areas)
2024 - 2030 (merged 'Physical Education and Arts' / Heritage-Based Curriculum syllabus)
meta.levels_covered: ECD A - Grade 7 (Infant: ECD A-Grade 2; Junior: Grade 3-7)
meta.learning_area_family: Visual and Performing Arts sits under the Arts pathway; Physical Education and Sport sits under Mass Displays/Sport; the two are combined at primary level and increasingly examined together as 'Physical Education and Arts' under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (HBC).
meta.notes: Zimbabwe's primary curriculum historically taught 'Visual and Performing Arts' and 'Physical Education, Sport and Mass Displays' as two related but separate learning areas (2015-2022 Curriculum Framework). Under the newer Heritage-Based Curriculum (HBC, syllabi rolled out 2024-2030), these were combined into a single 'Physical Education and Arts' (PE and Arts) syllabus for Infant and Junior levels, which integrates health, safety, the human body and physical fitness together with music, dance, theatre and visual arts. This file therefore documents both strands together as 'Health, Creative and Performing Arts', reflecting how the subject is actually taught in Zimbabwean primary schools.

rationale: Zimbabwe is endowed with cultural diversity, and it is imperative for learners to acquire visual and performing arts skills and competencies, as these are essential for self and national identity, entertainment, employment creation, problem-solving, critical thinking, creativity and self-discipline. Combined with Physical Education, the learning area also promotes physical, mental, emotional and social development, cultural heritage appreciation, healthy habits, teamwork and lifelong physical literacy. Music, dance, theatre and visual arts can lead to entrepreneurship, while physical education and sport prepare learners for both leisure and competitive participation and can be a means of livelihood.
aims: Develop understanding and appreciation of visual and performing arts (music, dance, theatre, visual arts) in their socio-economic, political and cultural context
Develop a positive interest in Visual and Performing Arts and Physical Education
Develop manipulative, hand-eye and foot-eye coordination, and other psychomotor skills
Promote physical fitness, healthy habits and lifelong participation in physical activity
Develop knowledge of safety, hygiene, the human body and disease prevention
Foster creativity, originality, critical thinking and problem-solving through the arts and sport
Instil teamwork, determination, leadership, self-discipline and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu values
Develop entrepreneurial/enterprising skills through the arts and sport (e.g. fundraising performances, careers in the arts)
Promote understanding and celebration of Zimbabwean cultural heritage through music, dance, theatre and visual arts
Provide equal opportunities for all learners, including those with different abilities, to reach their potential
assessment_objectives: Identify and operate simple musical, visual arts, theatre and dance tools and technologies appropriate to level
Demonstrate basic movement, rhythm, pitch and performance skills in music, dance and theatre
Produce simple visual artworks using appropriate media, tools and techniques
Describe and appreciate the history, culture and role of the arts in family, school, community and nation
Demonstrate safety awareness and injury-prevention practices during physical activities
Explain basic human body systems, hygiene and healthy-living practices
Participate in and demonstrate fundamental movement skills, games and physical fitness activities
Demonstrate enterprising/entrepreneurial skills and business ethics related to the arts and sport

arts_syllabus_topics.name: History and Culture
arts_syllabus_topics.description: The role of music, musicians, composers, visual artists, actors, dancers and their works in family, school, community and national culture, past and present.

arts_syllabus_topics.name: The Creative Process and Performance
arts_syllabus_topics.description: Practical creation and performance skills across music (pitch, rhythm, composition), visual arts (drawing, painting, modelling, crafting), theatre (story-telling, improvisation, tableau) and dance (movement patterns, sequences, group dynamics).

arts_syllabus_topics.name: Aesthetic Values and Appreciation
arts_syllabus_topics.description: Appreciating and critiquing artworks and performances; understanding elements/principles of design, meaning, mood and emotional response in art, music, theatre and dance.

arts_syllabus_topics.name: Arts Technology
arts_syllabus_topics.description: Use of technological tools in the arts - photography, video/filming, recording, ICT tools, lighting and sound effects, digital theatre, and internet ethics.

arts_syllabus_topics.name: Enterprising Skills (Entrepreneurship)
arts_syllabus_topics.description: Careers in the arts, business ethics, copyright protection, fundraising performances, exhibitions and commissioned work.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Human Body and Health
physical_education_health_topics.description: Body systems (e.g. digestion, respiration/breathing), personal hygiene, nutrition, growth and development.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Safety and Injury Prevention
physical_education_health_topics.description: Safety rules and regulations for physical activities and games; recognising and preventing common injuries; use of protective gear.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Fundamental Movement Skills
physical_education_health_topics.description: Running, jumping, balancing, throwing, catching, sprinting and other basic motor skills developed through games and gymnastics.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Games and Sports
physical_education_health_topics.description: Indigenous and modern children's games, team sports, athletics, and mass displays.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Healthy Living and Disease Prevention
physical_education_health_topics.description: Effects of physical inactivity and poor sanitation, disease prevention (including HIV/AIDS awareness), hydration and healthy habits.

physical_education_health_topics.name: Dance and Physical Expression
physical_education_health_topics.description: Movement patterns, rhythm and physical expression, overlapping with the Creative Arts strand.

infant_level_scope_and_sequence_arts.note: This is the official MoPSE scope-and-sequence table for Visual and Performing Arts at Infant level (ECD 0-3 years, ECD A, ECD B, Grade 1, Grade 2), showing how content spirals in depth across the levels. Each grade level list combines Music, Visual Arts, Theatre and Dance content for that topic.

ECD_0_3_years: Music: Musical instruments and sounds in the home; music in everyday life; movement in response to folk songs
Visual Arts: Visual arts in the home - eye movement to familiar colours/images, touching and feeling embossed material
Theatre: Mobiles; animation and puppetry in my home
Dance: Movement in response to folk songs; movement to sounds in everyday life experiences
ECD_A: Music: The role of music, musicians and composers in past and present cultures; musical instruments in my environment; songs and games in my home
Visual Arts: Visual arts in my home and culture; the role of visual arts and artists in my family; different types of visual arts past and present; safety with visual arts materials
Theatre: The role of theatre, animation and puppetry in my home and culture; characterisation - different family members and their roles; family stories
Dance: The role of dances and dancers in my home and culture; dance games
ECD_B: Music: The role of music/musicians/composers in past/present cultures; cultural diversity in music; movement in response to various instruments/genres/periods; songs and games in my school
Visual Arts: The role of visual arts and artists in my school; diversity in visual arts and artists; visual arts materials in the local environment
Theatre: The role of theatre, animation and puppetry in my school and culture; characterisation - different school members and their roles; school stories
Dance: The role of dances and dancers in my school and culture; folk dance and costumes
Grade_1: Music: The role of music/musicians/composers in past/present cultures; music and celebrations within Zimbabwe past and present; movements in response to instruments of different genres/periods/styles; songs and games in other cultures in my society
Visual Arts: The role of visual arts and artists in my community; works of art from a variety of places and times; visual arts materials from different cultures
Theatre: The role of theatre, animation and puppetry in my community and culture; characterisation - different community members and their roles; community stories
Dance: The role of dances and dancers in my community and culture; dance styles, costumes and music
Grade_2: Music: The role of music/musicians/composers in past and present cultures in daily and special events; movements in response to instruments of different genres/periods/styles; songs and games in my country
Visual Arts: The role of visual arts and artists in my country; functions of visual arts in daily life; visual arts objects and materials from different cultures

Theatre: The role of theatre, animation and puppetry in my country and culture; characterisation - different national leaders and their roles; national stories; roles and responsibilities of actors and audiences
Dance: The role of dances and dancers in my country and culture; social and cultural dances

topic_5_enterprise_skills.all_infant_levels_pattern: This topic follows a consistent structure across ECD A, ECD B, Grade 1 and Grade 2, deepening only in complexity of activity:

music: Business ethics (soft skills, Unhu/Ubuntu, copyright protection)
visual_arts: Media and tools (progressing from home, to school, to community, to country)
Business ethics (soft skills, Unhu/Ubuntu, copyright protection)
theatre: Business ethics (soft skills, Unhu/Ubuntu, copyright protection)
dance: Business ethics (soft skills, Unhu/Ubuntu, copyright protection)

sample_infant_lesson_plan.assumed_knowledge: Learners have seen and once played with some musical tools such as smartphones, TVs, picture puzzles etc.
objectives: Name video clips and pictures of different local artists
resources: Musical tools (radio, TV, smartphones, tape recorders, cassettes)
Books with pictures of musical tools

lesson_phases.activity: Guided discovery - teacher shows video/audio clips; learners watch, study pictures and listen to music performances by various artists and identify what they saw/heard.
Group work - learners explore pictures, photographs and videos of music performances and artists, then present their findings while the teacher reinforces answers.
Teacher asks summary questions on musical tools; learners respond and perform one song of their choice.

sample_junior_pe_content_grade6.note: Representative content from Grade 6 Physical Education/Health notes used in Zimbabwean primary schools under the Heritage-Based Curriculum.
safety_rules_and_regulations: Wear proper gear and equipment (e.g. helmets, knee pads)
Warm up and cool down before and after exercise
Follow rules and guidelines for each activity
Listen to your body and rest when needed
Ensure proper technique and use of equipment
healthy_living_topics: Effects of physical inactivity on the body
Effects of poor sanitation on health
The process of storing and transporting food in the body (digestion)
The process of transporting air in the body (respiration/breathing)
arts_topics_covered_alongside_pe_at_this: Zimbabwean music: cultural significance and evolution over time
Zimbabwean dance: cultural significance and evolution over time
Zimbabwean visual arts: cultural significance and evolution over time

recommended_teaching_methods.simulation_method: Imitation of a real or possible situation/process (e.g. simulating the liberation war, playing mahumbwe)

community_resources: Field trip venues (galleries, arts centres, studios)

assessment.mode: Continuous assessment supplemented by tests, projects, examinations and assignments
assessment.profiling: Learners are profiled to capture soft skills and practical/performance competencies not easily captured by written tests alone.
assessment.inclusivity_principle: Assessment must accommodate learners with special needs/different abilities so that all can access and demonstrate their competencies.
assessment.specification_grid: Used at national syllabus level to show proposed mark allocation across content areas (music, visual arts, theatre, dance, and PE/health strands) to ensure balanced syllabus coverage.

related_examinable_subjects_beyond_grade.note: From Form 1 onward, this combined primary learning area is carried into separate, more specialised ZIMSEC O-Level and A-Level subjects under the Visual and Performing Arts, and Physical Education/Sport pathways.
